question.prompt: The \(7\)-digit numbers \(\underline{74A52B1}\) and \(\underline{326AB4C}\) are each multiples of \(3\). Which of the following could be the value of \(C\)?

solutions.explanation:
A number is a multiple of \(3\) exactly when its digit sum is a multiple of \(3\). The two digit sums are
\[
19+A+B\quad\text{and}\quad15+A+B+C.
\]
Comparing them is useful because the shared digits \(A\) and \(B\) cancel. Since both sums are multiples of \(3\), their difference must also be a multiple of \(3\):
\[
(15+A+B+C)-(19+A+B)=C-4.
\]
Because \(C\) is a digit from \(0\) through \(9\), this restricts \(C\) to \(1,4,7\). Only \(1\) appears among the choices.

It is attainable: choosing \(A=0\), \(B=2\), and \(C=1\) gives digit sums \(21\) and \(18\), both multiples of \(3\). Thus \(C=1\) could occur, choice A.
solutions.title: Compare the two digit sums
